raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With the `vectorized_5d` KV-cache layout (`SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=vectorized_5d`) and an fp8 KV cache (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`), `MHATokenToKVPool.set_kv_buffer` divides K and V by their scales and casts them to fp8 in four elementwise launches per layer, and only then runs the 5D writer. This PR moves the divide and the cast into the 5D writer, which quantizes as it writes, so those four launches go away.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/kernels/ops/kvcache/shuffle_5d_cache.py`: the 5D writer takes optional K and V scales. With an fp8 cache it divides in fp32, saturates to the fp8 range as the other fused fp8 KV writes do, and casts. A scale may be a device tensor (read inside the kernel, so CUDA graph capture needs no host sync), a host tensor or a float. For a cache of the source's dtype the writer is unchanged.
- `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py`: with the `vectorized_5d` layout and an fp8 cache, `set_kv_buffer` hands the scales to the writer instead of quantizing first. The caller's K and V are no longer divided in place.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_shuffle_5d_fp8_write.py` (new, registered for AMD CI): checks the fused write against an fp32 divide, saturate and cast for each way of giving the scales, saturation past the fp8 range, and a bf16 round trip.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K, all 1319 questions (`python -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 1319 --parallel 128`), one MI355X (gfx950), TP 1, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=vectorized_5d`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`:

| Model | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | 0.756 | 0.744 |
| Qwen/Qwen3-8B | 0.905 | 0.904 |
| Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct | 0.025 | 0.033 |
| amd/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-FP8-KV | 0.000 | 0.010 |

The last two rows are already broken on main, and this PR does not change that. Controls on main, same setup:

| Model | NHD, bf16 KV | NHD, fp8 KV | vectorized_5d, bf16 KV | vectorized_5d, fp8 KV |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct | 0.873 | 0.027 | 0.871 | 0.025 |
| amd/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-FP8-KV | 0.952 | 0.948 | 0.948 | 0.000 |

- Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct fails with an fp8 KV cache in either layout, so its failure is not specific to `vectorized_5d`.
- Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-FP8-KV works with an fp8 KV cache in the NHD layout (0.948) and fails only with `vectorized_5d` plus fp8: 0.000 on main and 0.010 with this PR. That combination is broken on main independently of this change and needs its own fix.

Unit tests on the same image: the new `test_shuffle_5d_fp8_write.py` passes, and `test/registered/attention/test_aiter_fp8_kv_scales_paths.py` and `test/registered/attention/test_fused_fp8_kv_write.py` pass on main and on this branch.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`python -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random-ids --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 1.0 --max-concurrency C --num-prompts max(4C, 32)`, two runs per point (seeds 1 and 2), the mean shown. The server ran as above, with `--mem-fraction-static 0.85`. Each cell is main → this PR:

| Model | C | Output tok/s | Mean TPOT (ms) | Mean TTFT (ms) |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | 1 | 219.14 → 235.51 (+7.5%) | 4.46 → 4.14 (-7.1%) | 31.45 → 30.70 |
| | 16 | 2871.89 → 3168.26 (+10.3%) | 5.01 → 4.45 (-11.3%) | 144.50 → 154.33 |
| | 64 | 7592.76 → 8154.68 (+7.4%) | 6.24 → 5.69 (-8.9%) | 555.19 → 548.77 |
| Qwen3-8B | 1 | 206.03 → 223.72 (+8.6%) | 4.75 → 4.36 (-8.2%) | 32.06 → 33.49 |
| | 16 | 2691.23 → 2968.61 (+10.3%) | 5.34 → 4.81 (-9.8%) | 155.83 → 147.38 |
| | 64 | 6809.64 → 7258.22 (+6.6%) | 7.53 → 6.96 (-7.5%) | 478.26 → 473.44 |
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct | 1 | 239.48 → 254.78 (+6.4%) | 4.09 → 3.84 (-6.1%) | 26.42 → 25.10 |
| | 16 | 3192.16 → 3541.69 (+10.9%) | 4.56 → 4.08 (-10.4%) | 115.59 → 110.10 |
| | 64 | 8084.04 → 8705.19 (+7.7%) | 6.21 → 5.70 (-8.3%) | 432.50 → 419.92 |
| Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-FP8-KV | 1 | 55.52 → 59.33 (+6.9%) | 17.71 → 16.57 (-6.5%) | 93.30 → 89.78 |
| | 16 | 725.40 → 795.75 (+9.7%) | 19.95 → 17.97 (-9.9%) | 554.36 → 560.93 |
| | 64 | 1934.08 → 2085.19 (+7.8%) | 25.42 → 23.17 (-8.8%) | 1979.87 → 1938.76 |

The Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-FP8-KV rows show the write path's speed only; their accuracy in this configuration is broken on main (see above).

`python -m sglang.benchmark.one_batch --batch-size 1 16 64 --input-len 1024 --output-len 64` on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, median decode step, main → this PR: 4.77 → 4.50 ms at batch size 1 (-5.7%), 5.26 → 4.72 ms at 16 (-10.3%), 6.01 → 5.50 ms at 64 (-8.5%).

Setup: the `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm` rocm720-mi35x image of 2026-11-03 (aiter 0.1.26.dev144+g285579b62), with sglang from source. Measured with this commit on main at 045e0e2; it has been rebased onto 27aedf7 since, with the same diff under `python/`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No option or default changes.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+"""The SHUFFLE 5D KV writer's fused fp8 quantization: from bf16 K/V and
+per-tensor scales it writes what an fp32 divide, a saturation to the fp8 range
+and a cast would, for each way a scale can be given, and a cache of the
+source's dtype is written as before."""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_amd_ci
+
+register_amd_ci(est_time=12, stage="jit-kernel-unit", runner_config="amd")
+
+_HAS_GPU = torch.cuda.is_available()
+NUM_TOKENS, NUM_HEADS, HEAD_SIZE, BLOCK_SIZE, NUM_BLOCKS = 37, 8, 128, 16, 8
+
+
+def _caches(dtype: torch.dtype) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    x = 16 // torch.empty((), dtype=dtype).element_size()
+    shape_k = (NUM_BLOCKS, NUM_HEADS, HEAD_SIZE // x, BLOCK_SIZE, x)
+    shape_v = (NUM_BLOCKS, NUM_HEADS, BLOCK_SIZE // x, HEAD_SIZE, x)
+    return (
+        torch.zeros(shape_k, dtype=dtype, device="cuda"),
+        torch.zeros(shape_v, dtype=dtype, device="cuda"),
+    )
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(_HAS_GPU, "Triton kernels require a GPU")
+class TestShuffle5dFp8Write(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.quantization.fp8_kernel import fp8_dtype
+
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        self.fp8 = fp8_dtype
+        self.fp8_max = torch.finfo(fp8_dtype).max
+        shape = (NUM_TOKENS, NUM_HEADS, HEAD_SIZE)
+        self.k = 4 * torch.randn(shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        self.v = 4 * torch.randn(shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        slots = torch.randperm(NUM_BLOCKS * BLOCK_SIZE, device="cuda")
+        self.loc = slots[:NUM_TOKENS].to(torch.int64)
+
+    def _written(self, k_scale, v_scale) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+        """K and V read back from an fp8 cache the fused path wrote."""
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.kvcache.shuffle_5d_cache import (
+            launch_gather_shuffle_5d_to_linear,
+            launch_reshape_and_cache_shuffle_5d,
+        )
+
+        k_cache, v_cache = _caches(torch.uint8)
+        k_cache, v_cache = k_cache.view(self.fp8), v_cache.view(self.fp8)
+        launch_reshape_and_cache_shuffle_5d(
+            self.k, self.v, k_cache, v_cache, self.loc, k_scale=k_scale, v_scale=v_scale
+        )
+        return launch_gather_shuffle_5d_to_linear(k_cache, v_cache, self.loc)
+
+    def _expected(self, scale: float, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        # A one-element divisor, not a Python float: dividing by a Python float
+        # multiplies by its fp32 reciprocal, which differs from the kernel's
+        # fp32 divide in the last bit for a scale such as 0.03.
+        divisor = torch.tensor(scale, dtype=torch.float32, device=x.device)
+        return (x.float() / divisor).clamp(-self.fp8_max, self.fp8_max).to(self.fp8)
+
+    def _assert_matches(self, got: torch.Tensor, want: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+        self.assertFalse(torch.isnan(got.float()).any())
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(got.view(torch.uint8), want.view(torch.uint8)))
+
+    def test_each_way_of_giving_the_scales_writes_the_fp32_divided_values(self):
+        k_want, v_want = self._expected(0.05, self.k), self._expected(0.03, self.v)
+        ways = (
+            (0.05, 0.03),
+            (torch.tensor([0.05], device="cuda"), torch.tensor([0.03], device="cuda")),
+            (torch.tensor([0.05]), 0.03),
+        )
+        for k_scale, v_scale in ways:
+            with self.subTest(k_scale=k_scale, v_scale=v_scale):
+                k_got, v_got = self._written(k_scale, v_scale)
+                self._assert_matches(k_got, k_want)
+                self._assert_matches(v_got, v_want)
+
+    def test_values_past_the_fp8_range_saturate(self):
+        k_got, v_got = self._written(1e-4, 1e-4)
+
+        self._assert_matches(k_got, self._expected(1e-4, self.k))
+        self._assert_matches(v_got, self._expected(1e-4, self.v))
+        self.assertEqual(k_got.float().abs().max().item(), self.fp8_max)
+
+    def test_a_cache_of_the_source_dtype_is_written_as_given(self):
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.kvcache.shuffle_5d_cache import (
+            launch_gather_shuffle_5d_to_linear,
+            launch_reshape_and_cache_shuffle_5d,
+        )
+
+        k_cache, v_cache = _caches(torch.bfloat16)
+        launch_reshape_and_cache_shuffle_5d(self.k, self.v, k_cache, v_cache, self.loc)
+        k_got, v_got = launch_gather_shuffle_5d_to_linear(k_cache, v_cache, self.loc)
+
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(k_got, self.k) and torch.equal(v_got, self.v))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
